title: SET OF 6 COPELAND SPODE ENTREE...
reason: Set of six Copeland late Spode plates in the collectable blue leaf 'Cabbage' pattern (number reads 2/6207, about 1910s), which the title does not name.
findings: Six matching plates, each decorated with a large blue leaf with white dotted edge and red veins, pink and orange flowers, a blue branch border and a red-brown rim. Photo 2 shows the base of one plate with a printed blue cartouche mark reading 'COPELAND late SPODE ENGLAND' (the word ENGLAND puts it after 1891, and this Copeland late Spode mark ran well into the 20th century) plus a hand-painted red pattern number that is rotated and soft but reads as '2/6207', with a small extra red mark beside it (possibly a painter's or gilder's mark). Spode pattern 2/6207 is listed in Spode references as the 'Cabbage' pattern (a Tobacco Leaf style design) reissued on earthenware in 1910 to 1911, which matches the blue leaf with red and pink colouring seen. So the title's Copeland Spode is supported, while the pattern name and approximate date (about 1910s) are not in the title. Only one base was photographed, so the other five bases are unchecked, but all six fronts show the same pattern. Plate diameter is not stated and cannot be measured from the photos.
condition: No chips, cracks or rim damage visible on the fronts. Two plates show brownish staining or discolouration in the well (top left and bottom left), which may be tea staining with crazing. Some rubbing to the red edge line. Bases other than one not seen.
rescore_note: Six matching plates with a printed COPELAND late SPODE ENGLAND mark (so after 1891, probably 1910s) in a decorative blue leaf and floral pattern; good maker and a full set, held back by staining and crazing on two plates, only one base seen and a pattern number read from a soft rotated mark, so mid band.
